commit.message:
feat(cache_sync): account-scoped invalidation (#4361)

* feat(cache_sync): account-scoped invalidation + writeIfNewer (#4360)

Foundation PR for the data-foundation epic (#4335).

cache_sync gains two public methods:
  - `invalidatePrefix(prefix)` clears all entries whose key starts with
    the given prefix. Cache keys follow the `${pubkey}:operation`
    convention (RFC #4244) so calling with the leaving account's pubkey
    hex wipes that account without touching others on the same device.
  - `writeIfNewer<T>({key, value, fromJson, toJson, versionOf, ttl})`
    writes only when the new value's version is strictly greater than
    the cached value's (or when nothing is cached, or when the cached
    payload is corrupted). Intended for replaceable Nostr events
    (kinds 0, 3, 10000-19999, 30000-39999) where `created_at` ordering
    must be preserved across writes from multiple relays.

follow_repository's four cache-key helpers move from the legacy
`operation_${pubkey}` shape to RFC #4244's `${pubkey}:operation` so
prefix invalidation actually matches. One-time cache miss expected on
first launch post-PR (cache_sync only shipped 2026-05-11 in #4251).

AuthService.signOut now owns invalidation: it captures the current
pubkey and calls `CacheSync.invalidatePrefix(currentPubkey)` on both
destructive and non-destructive paths (previously only destructive ran,
via the wholesale `invalidateAll`). The `SettingsAccountCubit`
`invalidateAll` calls — which used to wipe every account's cache on
account switch / add-new — are gone. Multi-account users keep their
other accounts' caches for fast re-switch.

A small `@visibleForTesting void debugSetCurrentKeyContainer(...)` seam
is added to AuthService so the multi-account assertion test can exercise
the authenticated path without driving the full sign-in pipeline.

Closes #4360.

* fix(cache_sync): address review findings — LIKE escape, TOCTOU mutex, Crashlytics on invalidation failure (#4360)

Addresses senior-review + security-review findings on #4361:

- LIKE injection (B3 / sec-#2): `CacheDaoImpl.deletePrefix` now escapes
  `%`, `_`, `\` and uses `LIKE ?1 || '%' ESCAPE '\'` so the prefix is
  matched literally. Pubkey hex is unaffected today, but future
  non-pubkey callers (or user-controlled input) cannot accidentally
  over-delete or under-delete via wildcards. New tests pin `_`, `%`,
  and `\` round-tripping as literals.
- `invalidatePrefix('')` foot-gun (N4): asserts non-empty in debug;
  doc points callers to `invalidateAll()` for the wipe-everything case.
- TOCTOU race in `writeIfNewer` (B2 / sec-#3): two concurrent callers
  on the same key could both pass the version gate, with the slower
  writer overwriting the newer entry. The method now serializes
  per-key via an in-process completer chain so the read-compare-write
  triple is atomic. A new concurrency test demonstrates the race and
  pins the fix — it fails reproducibly without the mutex.
- Storage-failure visibility on signOut (sec-#5): `AuthService.signOut`
  now forwards `CacheSync.invalidatePrefix` exceptions to Crashlytics
  via the existing `_reportStorageError` path so a silent disk-residency
  regression is observable. The `try/catch` continues to keep signOut
  failure-tolerant. New test asserts signOut still reaches
  `AuthState.unauthenticated` when `deletePrefix` throws.
- `writeIfNewer` `_dao.read` throw contract (S2): pinned via test —
  storage-layer read failures are rethrown to the caller.
- Style + docs (S3 / S5 / N1 / N3): trimmed the 9-line comment in
  `auth_service.dart` to 3 lines; added trust-boundary warning + empty-
  toJson note to the `writeIfNewer` docstring; switched `on Object` to
  bare `catch (_)` for consistency.

Out of scope (deferred to follow-up sub-issues under #4335):
- Convention enforcement that all cache keys start with a pubkey
  (sec-#1) — belongs in M15 rules file + reviewer-enforceable lint.
- Test-seam consolidation for `debugSetIdentity` /
  `debugSetCurrentKeyContainer` (sec-#4 / S4) — cross-cuts existing
  code; separate follow-up.
- Legacy non-prefixed key migrator (sec-#6) — PR already documents
  the one-time miss; cache_sync only shipped 3 days ago and LRU
  bounds the residue to 100 MB.
- First production caller for `writeIfNewer` (B1) — explicitly the
  job of M2 / M4 / M16 in the M-series plan; the API is named
  infrastructure, not speculative.

* refactor(cache_sync): defer writeIfNewer to consumer PR (#4360)

Addresses @NotThatKindOfDrLiz's CHANGES_REQUESTED review on #4361:
land replaceable-event helpers with their first real caller instead of
as speculative infrastructure. Same change resolves the `Cache Sync CI`
failure — the four failing lints (comment_references, two
avoid_catches_without_on_clauses, unawaited_futures) were all inside
the removed `writeIfNewer` body.

Removed:
- `CacheSync.writeIfNewer<T>` static method
- `CacheSync._writeIfNewerLocks` per-key serialization map
- `cache_sync/test/cache_sync_write_if_newer_test.dart` (242 lines)

Net: -328 LOC. The M0 scope is now exactly what the PR title says:
account-scoped invalidation (`invalidatePrefix` + `signOut`
consolidation + `follow_repository` cache-key migration).

`writeIfNewer` is named infrastructure for M2 (OgViner) and M4
(PersonalEvent) per the #4335 M-series plan; it will land in the PR
that brings up its first real consumer.

* fix(cache_sync): runtime-enforce empty-prefix guard and drop unused invalidateAll (#4360)

Addresses @NotThatKindOfDrLiz's CHANGES_REQUESTED review on #4361
(commit 37a664d):

1. Empty-prefix guard on `invalidatePrefix` was a debug-only `assert`.
   In release builds the check disappears and `invalidatePrefix('')`
   flows through to `LIKE '' || '%' ESCAPE '\'`, full-wiping the
   cache — the exact blast-radius footgun this PR is trying to
   remove. Replaced the assert with a runtime-enforced
   `ArgumentError.value` so the guard cannot regress in release. Test
   updated to expect `ArgumentError` instead of `AssertionError`.

2. `invalidateAll()` had no production caller after this PR's signOut
   consolidation (AuthService.signOut uses
   `invalidatePrefix(currentPubkey)`; SettingsAccountCubit no longer
   calls it). Under the repo's no-new-tech-debt rule, removed the
   public method along with its underlying `CacheDao.deleteAll()`
   interface, `CacheDaoImpl.deleteAll()` implementation, and the
   `deleteAll()` stubs in `FakeCacheDao` and the three mobile test
   fakes (`feed_video_overlay_test`, `others_followers_screen_test`,
   `profile_header_widget_test`). The two `invalidateAll` test cases
   in `cache_sync_invalidate_test` and the `deleteAll` group in
   `cache_dao_test` are gone with the API.

3. `auth_service_signout_cleanup_test`: dropped the
   `_TrackingCacheDao.deleteAllCallCount` field plus its four
   assertions. Renamed the two "never calls CacheSync.invalidateAll"
   tests to describe what they actually pin — that an unauthenticated
   signOut skips cache invalidation entirely — using the surviving
   `deletePrefixCalls` assertion. The headline multi-account
   assertion (account B's cache survives an account A signOut)
   is unchanged.

Verification from mobile/:
- `dart format` — 0 files changed
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test packages/cache_sync` —
  No issues found
- `packages/cache_sync`: 67 / 67 tests pass (71 → 67 = the 4 removed
  `deleteAll`/`invalidateAll` cases)
- `auth_service_signout_cleanup_test`: 14 / 14 pass
- `packages/follow_repository`: 200 / 200 pass
- Touched widget tests (`feed_video_overlay`,
  `others_followers_screen`, `profile_header_widget`): all pass

* chore(cache_sync): doc + test polish from self-review (#4360)

- CacheDao.deletePrefix: interface doc now matches the implementation —
  escaping LIKE metacharacters is the implementation's responsibility,
  so callers can pass arbitrary string prefixes. Previous doc said
  "callers responsible for escaping", contradicting CacheDaoImpl.
- AuthService.debugSetCurrentKeyContainer: docstring caveat that this
  seam only mutates _currentKeyContainer, not _authSource /
  _currentIdentity / signer wiring / auth state. Safe for branches
  keyed solely on the current pubkey; not a general "pretend to be
  signed in" shim.
- auth_service_signout_cleanup_test throwing-deletePrefix case: also
  assert that A's seeded entries are still on disk. The fake throws
  before its removeWhere, so the contract being pinned is "failed
  invalidation leaves the cache in its pre-call state — no partial
  cleanup", not just "B's cache survives". Pre-existing assertion
  only checked B's entry, which would have been preserved either way.
